Six ways to wake up on the Pacific

A shortlist for Richie, built around one rule he set: you should see and hear the ocean from the room.

The brief

What Richie actually asked for

The hard rule
See and hear the ocean from the room, or at least from the hotel. A cliff view counts the same as being on the sand.
The feel
A proper beach vibe over a hotel with three bubble baths. Hotel or resort, never an Airbnb.
The days
Out in the city most days doing touristy walks and eating well, with a rental car and a few meet-ups.
The water
Up for kayaking, paddleboarding or a sail, and a dinner cruise is already on the list.
Ruled out
Pacific Beach and Mission Beach. Both are party central and wrong for this trip.
Budget
Not the deciding factor. Prices below are a relative scale so the trade-offs stay visible.

Four stretches of coast

They are not interchangeable

San Diego's coast changes character every few miles. Pick the stretch first, then the hotel.

La Jolla

Cove, village & the Shores

The most polished stretch of the coast, and it skews toward wealthy families. Cliffs and coves, sea lions barking at the Cove, kayak tours into the sea caves, and the densest run of good restaurants on the coast. Village parking is a pain.

20–25 min to downtown · 2 hotels shortlisted

North County

Del Mar through Encinitas

Del Mar is a small, upscale beach village. North through Solana Beach, Cardiff and Leucadia it turns surfy and relaxed, with cafés along Highway 101. The quietest stretch and the biggest getaway feeling.

30–40 min to downtown · 2 hotels shortlisted

Sunset Cliffs

Point Loma & Ocean Beach

Sandstone cliffs dropping straight into the surf, and the sunset spot locals name first. Almost no hotels, because it's nearly all houses. Ocean Beach next door is the funky bohemian surf town: a pier, taco shops, dive bars, a Wednesday farmers market.

15 min to downtown · 1 hotel shortlisted

Mission Bay

Vacation Isle & the bay parks

Flat calm water, resort islands, lawns and bike paths, and the most central base in the city. The catch is in the name. The water here is bay water: no surf sound and no Pacific view.

10–15 min to downtown · 1 hotel, with a caveat

The shortlist

Six hotels, six different trips

Ratings are Google's, with the review count. Fees are the hotel's own, and they are charged nightly on top of the rate.

La Jolla · 1003 Coast Boulevard

Pantai Inn

$$$$$ 4.4451 reviews 25rooms

Twenty-five rooms in a cluster of Balinese-style buildings on Coast Boulevard, closer to the water than anything else in the village. Ocean-view suites open onto private balconies, there's a rooftop deck for the sunset, and the seaside walking path to the Cove starts at the front door. Dinner is a two-block walk. It is the most romantic address on this list, and it knows it: there's a romance package with an in-room massage.

Ocean view
From the suites and the roof
Beach
Steps away, not on the sand
Walk to dinner
Yes, the whole village
Pool / restaurant
Neither on site
Fees
About $25 resort, $25 parking

Worth knowing. With no restaurant and no pool, everything except sleeping happens off the property, which suits a couple who'll be out all day.

Book an ocean-view suite →

La Jolla Shores · 2000 Spindrift Drive

La Jolla Beach & Tennis Club

$$$$$ 4.4807 reviews 1927founded

Twenty private acres on the sand, a mile and a half north of the village and a world away from it: residential, quiet, and fronting a long flat beach instead of the rocky cove. The same family has owned it since 1935. There are courts, a pool, fire pits on the sand, loungers and umbrellas set out for guests, and The Marine Room, where the waves hit the windows at high tide.

Ocean view
Beachfront rooms only
Beach
Private stretch, on the sand
Walk to dinner
No, it's a short drive
On site
Tennis, pool, The Marine Room
Fees
$68, parking included

Book the Beachfront category and nothing else. Those run from studios to three-bedroom suites, each with a patio or balcony on the sand. Every other category sits inland on the property with no stated view. Ground-floor units hear the surf all night, which most people love and light sleepers don't. A $60M renovation covers the resort and I could not confirm the second phase's dates, so ask.

Book a beachfront unit →

Del Mar · 1540 Camino Del Mar

L'Auberge Del Mar

$$$$$ 4.51,261 reviews 5.2acres

The splurge. An estate-style resort sitting in the middle of Del Mar village, with an ocean-view pool, a spa whose couples suite opens onto a private garden terrace with a soaking tub, and a private path down to the beach. Restaurants, boutiques and the village are outside the gate, which is the thing the other North County options can't offer.

Ocean view
From rooms and the pool
Beach
Private path down, not on sand
Walk to dinner
Yes, at the door
On site
Spa, pool, restaurant
Fees
$65 resort, $75 valet only

Worth knowing. $140 a night in fees before the room rate, and there is no self-parking option. The rooms sit up on the grounds rather than on the sand, so the view crosses the village on its way to the water.

Book an ocean-view room →

Del Mar · 1702 Coast Boulevard

Del Mar Beach Hotel

$$$$$ 4.4361 reviews 46rooms

The only hotel in Del Mar that is literally on the sand, and the reason it earns a place here despite being the simplest property on the list. Forty-six rooms facing the Pacific, beach chairs, umbrellas and boogie boards included, and the village a third of a mile up the road. It has been here since 1968 and was, until recently, the Del Mar Motel on the Beach.

Ocean view
Yes, rooms face the water
Beach
Directly on the sand
Walk to dinner
0.3 miles to the village
Rooms
Simple: fridge, coffee, TV
Fees
Not published

Set expectations on the rooms. This is a rebranded 1968 motel: the position is extraordinary, the rooms are plain. No restaurant, though two sit next door, and the site publishes nothing about a pool, a spa or its fees.

Book a room on the sand →

Point Loma · 1370 Sunset Cliffs Boulevard

The Inn at Sunset Cliffs

$$$$$ 4.5421 reviews 24rooms

Twenty-four rooms built out on the cliff edge in the 1950s and refreshed in 2018, with a small courtyard pool and the surf breaking on the rocks directly below. Nothing else on this list puts you this close to open water. Sunset Cliffs is where San Diego goes to watch the sun go down, and in November that happens just before five, right before dinner.

Ocean view
King Studio rooms only
Beach
Cliffs, not sand
Walk to dinner
Ocean Beach, a short walk
On site
Pool, no restaurant or spa
Published rates
$200–$375 a night

Book the King Studio, Upper or Lower. Those are the rooms advertised with a full ocean and cliff view. The poolside queens and kitchen suites have no stated view, so ask for the studio by name.

Book a King Studio →

Mission Bay · 1404 Vacation Road

Paradise Point

$$$$$ 4.24,889 reviews 462rooms

The one Richie asked about by name, and the best of the Mission Bay resorts: a 44-acre island of single-storey bungalows with private patios, five heated pools including one for adults only, a full spa, five restaurants and a mile of its own sand. It is also the cheapest place on this list by a wide margin, and it is genuinely beautiful.

Ocean view
None, anywhere on site
Water
Flat bay, warm and calm
Walk to dinner
On site, five restaurants
On site
Five pools, spa, bay beach
Fees
$46 resort, $49 parking

Read the water before you book. Paradise Point sits entirely inside Mission Bay, so there is no Pacific view from any room and you will never hear surf. The sand is bay sand, flat and calm, which is ideal for a paddleboard. Taken on its own terms this is a lovely few days: a private patio on a quiet island, an adults-only pool, a spa and dinner without moving the car. It simply doesn't do the one thing Richie asked for.

Things worth doing

November is the quiet month

The summer crowds have gone home and the water is still warm this year. Late-afternoon light in November is the best San Diego gets.

On the water

Start here

  • Kayak the La Jolla sea cavesGuided two-hour tour through the seven caves inside the ecological reserve, with sea lions on the rocks and often in the water with you. Runs year-round, weather permitting.Bike and Kayak Tours · from $59 per kayak · no wetsuit needed
  • Paddleboard Mission BayFlat, protected water and the easiest possible first attempt on a board. Rent by the hour on Santa Clara Place.Mission Bay Sportcenter · rentals by the hour
  • Humpback whale watchingMid-October through November is humpback season aboard the schooner America. Gray whales don't arrive until December, so this is the window they actually get.Next Level Sailing · $86.40 per adult · 3 hours
  • A private sunset sailTwo hours on the bay with a captain, usually with champagne. Several operators run near-identical charters from Harbor and Shelter Island.From about $279–600 per charter · confirm November rates

Dinner on the water

The one he liked the sound of

  • City Cruises dinner cruiseNightly three-course dinner cruise around the bay, past the Coronado Bridge, the Midway and the skyline. Two and a half hours on weeknights, three at weekends.Boards at 990 N Harbor Dr · roughly $85–119 per person, drinks extra
  • Flagship harbor dinner cruiseThe alternative, from the same terminal cluster. Weeknight and Saturday sailings at 7:30pm, Sundays at 6:30pm.Confirm the November schedule directly
  • The Marine Room, at high tideNot a cruise, but the closest you can eat to the Pacific without getting in it: waves break against the windows. Check the tide chart and book that hour.La Jolla Shores · reserve well ahead

Culture, this particular week

Dated to their trip

  • GRIM at La Jolla PlayhouseA world-premiere musical about the Grim Reaper's daughter falling in love with life, running October into November at the Weiss Theatre on the UCSD campus.The one Playhouse show inside their dates
  • The Grinch at The Old GlobeOpens November 8, their arrival day, and runs through December in Balboa Park. Festive rather than romantic, but it's the Globe at its most San Diego.Balboa Park · Nov 4 – Dec 31
  • Balboa Park museumsThe Timken is free and holds European masters and Russian icons. The Mingei does craft and design, and the Natural History Museum is next door. An unhurried afternoon, all walkable.Check each museum's own hours
  • San Diego Bay Wine + Food FestivalRuns November 1–8, so it catches only their first day. Worth a look if anything on the Sunday lineup appeals.Overlaps day one only

Classic San Diego

The ones that earn the drive

  • Safari ParkThe better half of the zoo operation: 1,800 acres where the animals have the space and you ride through it. About 45 minutes inland from the coast.$78 per adult · Escondido
  • Torrey Pines State ReserveCliff-top trails dropping to the beach, between La Jolla and Del Mar. Gates open 7:15am to sunset. The lodge building closed for construction in September, the trails did not.Parking $15–25 · no dogs, no picnics
  • Cabrillo National MonumentThe lighthouse and tide pools at the very end of Point Loma, looking back across the whole bay. Open 9 to 5 daily.$20 per vehicle
  • Sunset Cliffs at golden hourFree, and ten minutes from the harbor. Luscomb's Point is the lookout. Get there before 4:30pm in November.No fee · two small dirt lots that fill fast
  • Little Italy MercatoSix blocks of farmers market on Saturday mornings, a smaller version on Wednesdays, year-round.Sat 8am–2pm · Wed 9:30am–1:30pm

Something they won't expect

The ones worth arranging

  • A styled pop-up picnic on the cliffsA low table, cushions and a proper spread, set up for you at Sunset Cliffs or La Jolla and cleared away after. Several San Diego companies do it, all by quote, with about 48 hours' notice.Pricing by consultation only
  • Mahjong nightSan Diego has a real mahjong scene: beginner-friendly Zung Jung on Wednesdays and Fridays for $5, and a coastal club that plays in La Jolla village.Check the Meetup calendar for that week
  • Couples spa at L'AubergeSide-by-side treatments in a suite that opens onto a private garden terrace with a soaking tub. Worth doing even if they stay elsewhere.Del Mar · rates by enquiry
  • Stargazing on Mount LagunaAn hour east, 6,000 feet up, no city light. October to mid-November is one of the two best windows of the year, so their week lands right in it.Free · bring layers, it's cold up there
  • Hot air balloon over Del MarSunset flights over the valley and the coast, about an hour up, champagne included. Call first: the season runs spring to early autumn and November flights are not confirmed.From $300 per person · confirm before planning around it

Where to eat

One standout per area

  • NINE-TENLa Jolla's special-occasion room: a chef-driven seasonal tasting menu in a warm, low-lit space in the village.La Jolla village
  • Bali HaiOld-school tiki on Shelter Island, with the skyline across the water doing the heavy lifting.Point Loma
  • Jake's Del MarRight at the sand, best at sunset, good for a long lunch after a beach morning.Del Mar
  • Aqua MareItalian with a lagoon and ocean view, quieter and more grown-up than the beach-front places.Del Mar
